Dear Mom,
(opening omitted)
I'm sorry, Mom. You must be so disappointed in me. In the end I didn't dare sign up. You said my grades were good enough... but my luck has always been terrible. Little Flybug's takeoff success rate is still low, and even if it does barely get airborne, if it loses control at the venue and knocks the professor's wig flying, or (a long stretch of writing blurred by water stains)—you know how unlucky I always am. But you were right. I'll watch my classmates and my professors more closely and see how they solve it.
(closing omitted)
My dearest, dearest Mom,
You won't believe it! The day after I mailed my last letter, I went and signed up for the competition~ It started with a small flash of inspiration: I improved Little Flybug's wings and just barely pushed its takeoff success rate up to—fifty percent... And then I tried my classmates' methods: setting Fluid Dynamics on my lap, repainting the core components cherry red, counting to seven before hitting the switch. I could feel it—the success rate was definitely a little higher than fifty percent! Correcting for luck is part of science too, right? Heheh. So I couldn't help myself, and I signed up.
(closing omitted)
My good, kind Mom,
I never thought you'd worry enough to write to Dad on purpose and ask him to cheer me on as well. Don't worry, it's not that I lack confidence, and it's certainly not superstition! It's just that if success and failure are each fifty-fifty, then the moment I step out there the result is guaranteed to land in the failing half. And my technique still isn't good enough, so what am I supposed to do... At the very least, doing a little ritual before every experiment sets my mind at ease. It feels a bit like when I was small and my friends laughed at me for getting my hands filthy from welding, and you patted my back and told me not to cry—heheh. Of course, I'll keep improving my design too, so please don't worry.
Wait—it just hit me, I'm not allowed to do any of those extra things at the competition! Why didn't I think of that when I signed up, aaaah! I'm doomed... (writing blurred by water stains)
(closing omitted)
Mom!
You've seen the award certificate I sent along with this letter by now, haven't you? I'm so glad it arrived safely! Do you know what happened? Little Flybug lifted right off, steady as anything, in full view of the judges and the audience! Repainting it cherry red, hiding a control valve in my pocket, eating my carrots with the skins on at breakfast—those really do bring good luck! But... I've also started to hope, just a little. Could it be that every time I improved the technology, the other fifty percent of possibility shrank toward nothing? Could it be that what makes up for a shortage of luck is, in fact, my own skill? Could it even be that someday I might really amount to something?
Ugh... I always start dreaming big the moment things go a little my way. One ought to stay humble, stay careful! But surely it's all right to dream once in a while. You'll dream along with me, won't you, Mom?
...Of course, I'll keep doing my little rituals. Even progress in engineering needs a bit of luck, heheh.
